summary:
This L0009 run started at 08:01 UTC on Nov 27 from the line's timer. There was no instruction for it (instructions/ has nothing after Nov 23), so it had no 'Asked' items and the empty answers list is right. It made no claims and changed none. It built two fixes on branch method/rest: side walls as contacts of a moving stack, with the wall crossing found exactly (D0098, f397ada), and handling for restarting a stack paused at a step's end (D0099, 0cd6a2b). It tested them in E0111 (supported) and E0113 (falsified). It also traced the cost of the frequency 0.4 layer (E0112, supported) and ran that layer long enough to reach the point the last run's pull rule was aimed at (E0110, supported). This time the git history is linear: no reset or rewrite in the reflog, and every registration was committed before its run's data. The main problem is one inflated count. The pinned page is also stale again on the frequency 0.4 layer.

(1) 'The pull rule acted 43 times' counts the final loop's repeats as uses of the rule (E0110). The summary, the outcome, the line state ('the pull rule acted 43 times') and the progress file all say the rule acted 43 times: 35 pulling contacts dropped at stack starts and 8 opened at restarts. But the run ends in a same-instant loop of 31 calls in which sphere 54 touches stack sphere 59 again and again. The run's own list of touch approach speeds ends with 30 touches below 1e-10, all at that instant (38 in the whole run). I read the stack-hit handler (granular/sim.py, _on_stack_hit and _stack_new at 975a4d7). In a join that succeeds, sphere 54 becomes part of sphere 59's stack, and the two can't touch again. For them to touch again at the same instant, something must separate them. The loop could not have gone through refused starts (0), splits (6 in the whole run) or openings (8). The only counter large enough is pull_dropped. That is the path where the new contact pulls, is dropped, the parts start separately, and the event search then sees the round-off approach as a fresh touch. So about 30 of the 35 'drops' are very likely the loop repeating. The rule's real uses before the loop are then about 5 drops and the 8 openings, roughly 13, not 43. Also, pull_dropped is shared with the older drop-at-start rule (D0091), so not every drop is the newer rule's. I did not rerun E0110 to confirm this, because it needs 29 minutes of CPU, more than my ten-minute limit; this rests on the code and the run's own records. What stands: start_refused is 0, the layer passed 5.276 and completed the step to 5.28, and the openings (pull_opened 8) can only come from the newer rule. So 'the rule works where it was aimed' holds in substance. The count is wrong, and so is the loop's description. The summary calls the loop 'a touch at round-off speed, each handled as a join', of the kind D0092 fixed inside a stack. It looks more like the drop rule and the event search disagreeing: the drop says the two spheres separate by their accelerations, but the search counts the leftover round-off approach as a new touch. That points the next fix at the drop path, not only at a touch floor.

(2) The pinned page, lines/L0009/pinned/current-algorithm.md, is stale on the frequency 0.4 layer again. It was last committed at 08:34:52 (a4ab259), before E0110 finished at 08:43. The later commit 0e139e4 brought the line state, progress and PROGRAM.md up to date with E0110, but not the pinned page. The page still says 'seed 1, f* 0.4 to 5.27 at 848 s CPU (E0109)'. The evidence says that layer completed the step to 5.28 and then looped at 5.2816. Its header names method/rest f397ada, but the branch tested last is 0cd6a2b (D0099). This is the same kind of fault as point (3) of my last review.

(3) Line state for L0009 (the 08:44:08 update). Most of it holds. Two sentences are wrong. 'seed 1 at f* 0.4 now gets past its pulling contacts (the pull rule acted 43 times)' should give about 13 uses, as in point (1). The next sentence, 'That cost is the linear solve for the contact forces', now has nothing to refer to: the edit took out the phrase 'limited by cost' that it pointed back to. It should say the frequency 0.4 layer's slowness is that solve. The note's sentences hold.

What reproduces. I reran E0111 seed 1 at f* 0.3 (from a clean copy of f397ada) and E0113 (from 0cd6a2b) with the session's script and settings. Both match the recorded result files in every field except CPU times. Every one of the 592 step lines matches. Both stop where the session says: 'stack start: conditions violated [12]' at 5.92 for E0111, and 'rider and free sphere overlap' at 5.92 for E0113, with 2 splits and 7 openings. All ten data files in runs/E0110 to runs/E0113 match their recorded sizes and SHA-256. The summary's numbers appear in the evidence files: 1360 s to complete 5.28 and the loop at 5.2816; 5 wall cuts and 2 joins at a wall; 99.1% of stack CPU (489.6 of 493.9 s) in force solves; 9.1 solves per integrator step; 14.0 steps per stored piece in the 185 s call; 7,299 solves for 57 pieces.

Did the changes act? D0098 did. Its wall counters are above zero in seed 1, and the step log differs from E0109's first in the step to 5.92. In seed 2 it never acted (no wall cut), and that layer's run is identical to E0109, as the session says. To check the claim that the wall penetration is 'removed at its source', I ran seed 1 at f* 0.3 with a wrapper that records every sphere's distance past a side wall at each step end. Before D0098 (975a4d7), no sphere was past a wall at any step end; the 1.5e-7 penetration happened inside the step that then looped, where a check at step ends can't see it. After D0098 (0cd6a2b), no sphere was past a wall at any of the 592 step ends. At the last one, sphere 92, the one that was past the wall in E0109, sits exactly on the wall as a stack sphere. That supports the claim at step ends; inside a step it rests on the bisection, which I read and which looks right. D0099 acted at least once: E0111's unhandled error is now a split. The other split and the five extra openings in E0113 happened after the point where E0111 stopped. So comparing them with E0111 'at the same stop point' compares the new path with no path, not with the old one.

E0112, the cost trace. Its conclusion holds: the time goes to force solves, not to a loop. The per-call records show one more cost the summary leaves out. Five handler calls happen at the same instant, t = 5.251078: a sphere joins a 2-sphere stack, then a 3-sphere, then a 4-sphere, then a 5-sphere one. Each join integrates the whole stack again from that instant, at 29, 78 and 185 s. So about 300 of the 494 s are spent redoing a stack's integration as spheres join it one at a time at the same moment. Making each solve cheaper helps, but joining all touches at the same instant at once would remove most of that call's cost. The summary's 'two causes' could add this as a third.

Smaller points. (a) The summary disclosed that the E0111 outcome line was first appended as 'falsified' and corrected before any commit. Git confirms that only the corrected line was ever committed, so no committed record changed. Editing an uncommitted ledger line is within the rules, but it is worth knowing. (b) The commit f397ada on method/rest lacks the attribution line, as disclosed. (c) The experiments' prose names decision D0092, against the rule of no ids in that prose. (d) The approach speeds of 1e-16 are described as fractions of a 'sound-speed scale'. The model has no sound speed; the velocity unit is presumably the square root of gravity times a sphere diameter.

Last review's points. (1) The history rewrite: not repeated. The reflog for this run shows only commits. Chris's decision on the earlier rewrite is still open, and the map still shows the old E0106 and E0107 numbers. (2) The E0109 frequency 0.4 clause that never reached D0095: answered by E0110, which ran long enough (2100 s cap) and wrote down beforehand that stopping before 5.276 would count as 'not tested'. (3) The pinned page's three stale points: all three fixed (plate landing acted once, 6.59, frequency 0.4 to 5.27), but it went stale again, as in point (2). (b) of last review, the wall penetration: taken up as D0098 and checked above.

Claims. None proposed or changed, and none under an open challenge on this line. The experiments were checked against the failure modes. Energy injection: max_gain is 0 and the engine's energy-gain counter is 0 in every layer. The largest touch gain is 1.2e-15 (E0110), round-off. No layer finished a cycle, so there is no audit to recompute. The 'tuned to the test case' and 'easy cases only' failure modes don't apply to bug fixes that don't yet survive any layer.

Housekeeping. program check passes. The latest approval is approved/20261124T031934, more than a day old. The data folder is 746 megabytes of the 15 gigabyte limit, with 76 gigabytes free against a floor of 40. tmp/ is empty and active.jsonl is empty. Nothing was written outside the program folders between 08:00 and 08:48. My scratch folder checker/ has been removed.

Work nobody asked for: none. With no instruction, every experiment followed the line's own 'next' or my last review's points.

run_conditions.assessment: The run started at 08:01:43, 43 seconds after its scheduled time, and made its last commit at 08:46:21, within the hour. It built and tested two fixes, ran a cost trace, and answered the last review's main open point, so a lot got done. The machine did not limit the science: 76 GB free, the data folder under 1 GB, and low load. The recorded 1.13 CPU-hours matches the sum of the runs' own CPU times (1751 + 1079 + 682 + 283 + about 290 s is 4085 s, or 1.13 h). Sleep could not be checked, because pmset and ps are absent on this Linux worker.
discrepancies: The summary's 'ended' is 08:44:39, but two later commits fixing the summary's schema fields were made at 08:45:40 and 08:46:21.
The line state and summary say the pull rule acted 43 times. About 30 of those are very likely repeats of the final same-instant loop, not separate uses (see summary, point 1).
